title: ChopGate — a gate between your AI agent and your money

footerLimits: Testnet only. Mainnet: not deployed. Not audited. No real funds. This page never asks you to paste a key.
homeH1: A gate between your AI agent and your money.
homeSub: A NEAR smart contract holds the money you set aside for your agent. It pays only for jobs you signed. Any other request is refused: nothing is paid, and the reason is recorded on-chain.
homeCap1: An AI agent wants to spend your money. Nothing is stamped yet, so the gate refuses.
homeCap2: You stamp (sign) each job it may pay for: recipient, maximum amount, exact instruction.
homeCap3: The agent asks for exactly that job, within your limit: paid.
homeCap4: A different instruction, a fake owner, or a higher amount: refused, and recorded.
homeCap5: Above the review amount you set, a payment waits for your approval.

homeVerdictsTitle: Every payment request ends in one of three ways
homeVerdictPaidText: Testnet NEAR leaves the gate only for a stamped job.
homeVerdictHeldText: Above your review amount, the payment waits for your approval. After the deadline (one hour at most) it can no longer be approved, and nothing is paid.
homeVerdictRefusedText: Nothing is paid. The transaction itself goes through and stores a reason code on-chain, so anyone can check what the agent tried.
homeChecksTitle: Up to three checks, in order
homeCheck1Text: Stamped jobs, limits and budgets are checked on-chain.
homeCheck2Text: An optional second check: a judge model reviews the request before payment. Used live in testnet Run B (see Proof).
homeCheck3Text: Payments above your review amount wait for you.

homeStat2: paid on the refused requests among them
homeStat3: attack requests you can send yourself from a testnet wallet
homeLimit2: Not deployed on mainnet. No real funds.
homeLimit3: The stamp key (the key you sign jobs with) cannot be changed later. Back it up before you deposit.
homeLimit4: Anyone who knows a mandate serial can freeze it with the same refused request from the same account twice in a row (with no passing request in between), or three mandate-check refusals in a row. Nothing is paid, a new mandate recovers use, and that mandate can be frozen again. The refusal count goes back to 0 only when a request passes the mandate checks with an amount above 0 and the transaction does not fail, whatever follows: a payment, a new hold, a spend-rule refusal (tier2_deny), or an allowed request that pays nothing (an authorize call or an action other than a transfer). A zero-amount request leaves the count unchanged. Approving or rejecting a hold later does not change it.
homeLimit5: Anyone can grow the gate's storage with refused requests that carry long strings: in the sandbox, 3 requests grew storage by 63,758 bytes, and a full escrow withdrawal then failed with LackBalanceForState, about 0.028 NEAR short. A plain NEAR transfer (not Deposit) of the shortfall fixes it. There is no per-mandate storage cap in the contract (a 4th call on an already frozen mandate added 0 bytes in that run), and the fix is designed, not deployed.
homeStampWarn: If you lose the stamp key you cannot take the escrow out. It is stored in this browser without encryption.
homeWhyDesc: Without a gate, an AI agent that holds your wallet key can follow hidden text in a web page and send all your money to an attacker. With ChopGate the agent can only ask the gate: the hidden request is refused and nothing is paid, while the job you stamped, 0.01 NEAR to translator.testnet, is paid.
